reason: The cited evidence (E1) confirms that thermal exposure of the FeCoNiMnCu HEA in air at 800°C forms a high-entropy spinel oxide and increases hardness, supporting the first three premises. However, E1 provides no data on tribo-corrosion, dynamic removal/reformation of the oxide, or its simultaneous effect on wear and corrosion, leaving the last two premises unsupported by the cited passage.
premises: The equiatomic FeCoNiMnCu HEA forms a high-entropy spinel oxide (Fe,Co,Ni,Mn,Cu)3O4 upon thermal exposure in air at 800°C.
This spinel oxide forms as a continuous protective layer on the alloy surface.
The spinel oxide layer contributes to increased hardness.
The spinel oxide layer can form and reform dynamically under combined wear and oxidation conditions.
The dynamic oxide layer simultaneously reduces both wear and corrosion during tribo-corrosion.
